test: two-force decomposition (design.md §RQ, Abstract B) on the MV-B transplant panel
why: MV-B independently varied designer SIZE (2.5-9B) and designer FAMILY (same vs cross) on the SAME targets. Every previous cross-self contrast in this program confounded the two: 'cross' designers were often a different size from the target's own 3B self arm. This is the first fit that separates them.
spec: removal ~ log2(designer_size) + same_family + is_self, with target x axis CELL fixed effects

log2(designer size).reading: matching benefit: doubling designer size adds ~0.042 removal

same_family.reading: a same-family LARGE designer behaves like a cross-family one; no family penalty

is_self.reading: additional deficit when designer IS the target, beyond same-family; marginal

interpretation: Of the 'two opposing forces' the design posits, only the matching benefit (designer scale) is reliably present. The family-categorical penalty is absent once size is controlled (+0.006). What little remains is SELF-specific (-0.063, CI touching 0), not family-specific: total self-vs-cross effect = +0.006 - 0.063 = -0.057.
caveats: 6 cells, cluster-bootstrapped over cells — wide intervals
is_self rests on 3 designer-cells per cell (one self designer x 3 seeds)
MV-B panel lacks the two nulls (§1); same caveat as the panel itself
cells are heterogeneous (phi-occ +0.288 vs gemma-occ -0.174); the fit reports the average, and the average conceals real per-cell variation
